sentences.text: Mirarce eatoni is the sole species within the genus Mirarce, a group of enantiornithine birds from the Late Cretaceous of Utah. The name translates to 'wonderful winged messenger'.
This bird grew to be around two feet tall, making it similar in size to a modern Turkey vulture.
Its anatomy featured a humerus that was short and strong.
Quill knobs, the first such structures ever found in enantiornithines, were preserved on the ulna of Mirarce eatoni.
Paleontologist Howard Hutchison discovered the fossil remains of Mirarce in Utah in 1992.
Mirarce belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes and is classified as a member of the family Avisauridae, closely related to Avisaurus.
The genus Mirarce was established by Atterholt et al. in 2018.

Mirarce fossils have been found in the Kaiparowits Formation of western North America from the late Campanian age of the Cretaceous. Mirarce lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
